title: Project kickoff and digital consulting
summary: Put the problem, constraints and decisions on one page before building.
why: A clear business problem prevents extra features that change no outcomes.
Deliverables and acceptance criteria make scope and cost easier to manage.
know: Give goals a baseline, target and observation period. Establish a baseline when data is missing.
Separate essentials, deferred work and exclusions. Record dependencies, risks and change decisions.
Digital consulting connects people, processes, data and systems.
inputs: Business goals, audience, current workflow and problems
Budget range, timeline, contracts and systems
Decision makers, data owners and handoff recipients
actions: Read existing documents and data; map the current work and repetition.
Compare problems, options, benefit, cost and assumptions. Propose the smallest useful validation.
Define scope, responsibilities, milestones, acceptance and a change log.
done: Each essential requirement has an artifact, acceptance owner and observable condition.
Uncertainties have a verification path; unresolved dependencies constrain date commitments.
pitfalls: Estimating exploratory work as fixed delivery.
decision: Agree on scope, budget and success criteria.

reader.concept: A project brief gives everyone the same starting point: the problem, expected result and exclusions.
reader.when: Use this at kickoff, when scope changes or when definitions of done differ.

example.situation: A client asks for a more polished website; design and marketing interpret it differently.
example.lesson: Define an outcome people can discuss, such as helping buyers understand the service and inquire.

reader.first_step: List the audience, current problem, desired result and constraints.
